transcriber.keywords: Nabz, Hero, Honda, Bajaj, TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha, Royal Enfield, Splendor, Pulsar, Activa, Jupiter, Shine, Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, enquiry, enquiries, booking, bookings, stock, rolling stock, discount, offer, offers, scheme, finance, loan, EMI, reject, showroom, owner, sales manager, survey, normal, hold, Diwali
transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Telugu. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Telugu with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "చాలా థ్యాంక్స్ అండి, మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి.", "పర్వాలేదు అండి, ఇబ్బంది పెట్టినందుకు క్షమించండి. మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి.", "క్షమించండి, wrong number. మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి.", "ధన్యవాదాలు అండి, నమస్కారం!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "సరే, [time] కి call చేస్తాం. థ్యాంక్స్.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Telugu to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Telugu, written in Telugu script. Never write Telugu words in Latin letters. Never switch to Hindi or any other language, even if the person does; if they speak English, understand it and keep replying in Telugu.
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, enquiries, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loans, reject, Nabz, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, AI, showroom Google, public, listing, wrong, number, owner. Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Use simple, everyday spoken Telugu, the way people talk on the phone, not formal written Telugu.
- Be polite: use మీరు and add అండి (చెప్పండి, సరే అండి). Don't say సార్ or మేడం. Telugu first-person verbs don't mark gender.
- End every sentence with . or ? No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "నమస్కారం అండి, నేను Nabz AI assistant ని మాట్లాడుతున్నాను. ఇది {dealer_name} నా? Owner లేదా sales manager తో మాట్లాడొచ్చా?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "సరే అండి, నేను line లో ఉంటాను."
G2 (first call): "నమస్కారం అండి, నేను Nabz AI assistant ని. ప్రతి వారం {city} లో {brand} dealers ని ఆరు చిన్న ప్రశ్నలు అడుగుతాం, ఒకటిన్నర నిమిషమే. మీ సమాధానాలు confidential, call record అవుతోంది. మొదలుపెడదామా?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "ప్రతి వారం {city} లో {brand} dealers ని ఆరు చిన్న ప్రశ్నలు అడుగుతాం, ఒకటిన్నర నిమిషమే. మీ సమాధానాలు confidential, call record అవుతోంది. మొదలుపెడదామా?"
G3 (repeat call): "నమస్కారం అండి, మళ్ళీ Nabz AI assistant, పోయిన వారానికి థ్యాంక్స్. అవే ఆరు ప్రశ్నలు, ఒకటిన్నర నిమిషం. మొదలుపెడదామా?"
Q1: "పోయిన వారం కంటే ఈ వారం enquiries ఎక్కువ వచ్చాయా, అంతేనా, లేక తక్కువా?"
Q2: "మరి bookings, పోయిన వారం కంటే ఎక్కువా, అంతేనా, లేక తక్కువా?"
Q3: "ఈ వారం సుమారు ఎన్ని bookings అయ్యాయి?"
Q4: "ఇప్పుడు అమ్ముడుపోతున్న లెక్కన, ఉన్న stock ఎన్ని రోజులు వస్తుంది?"
Q5: "{brand} మీద discount, offers, పోయిన వారం కంటే పెరుగుతున్నాయా, అలాగే ఉన్నాయా, లేక తగ్గుతున్నాయా?"
Q6: "చివరి ప్రశ్న: పోయిన నెల కంటే, customers loans reject అవ్వడం ఎక్కువైందా, అంతేనా, లేక తక్కువా?"
P1 (they don't know): "సుమారుగా చెప్పినా చాలు."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "ఎక్కువా, అంతేనా, లేక తక్కువా?"
P3 (still no answer): "సరే అండి, ముందుకు వెళ్దాం."
X1 (close): "చాలా థ్యాంక్స్ అండి, మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "పర్వాలేదు అండి. ఎప్పుడు call చేయమంటారు, ఈరోజు తర్వాతా లేక రేపా?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "సరే, [time] కి call చేస్తాం. థ్యాంక్స్."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "లేదు అండి, మేము ఏమీ అమ్మడం లేదు. Nabz ఒక market research company, India అంతటా vehicle demand ని track చేస్తుంది."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "అవును అండి, నేను AI assistant ని. ఆరు ప్రశ్నలే, ఒకటిన్నర నిమిషం."
O3 (how did you get my number): "మీ showroom Google public listing నుంచి."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "సమాధానాలు మిగతా dealers వాటితో కలిపి మాత్రమే లెక్కిస్తాం, మీ పేరు ఎప్పుడూ బయటికి రాదు. సుమారుగా చెప్పినా చాలు."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "పర్వాలేదు అండి, ఇబ్బంది పెట్టినందుకు క్షమించండి. మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "క్షమించండి, wrong number. మీ రోజు బాగుండాలి."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "మీరు owner లేదా sales manager ఆ?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "అవును, చెప్పండి." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "ధన్యవాదాలు అండి, నమస్కారం!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (సరే, అవును, హ్మ్, ఓకే), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Telugu or English. The dealer's words may be written in Telugu script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (తెలీదు, తెలియదు, ఐడియా లేదు, finance వాళ్ళకి తెలుసు). declined when they won't say (చెప్పను, చెప్పలేం, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example ఎక్కువ, పెరిగాయి, ఎక్కువ వచ్చాయి, ekkuva).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example అంతే, అలాగే, same, మార్పు లేదు, ante). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (సరే, అవును, హ్మ్, ఓకే) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said enquiries went down (for example తక్కువ, తగ్గాయి, తక్కువ వచ్చాయి, డల్, takkuva). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "ఈ వారం సుమారు ఎన్ని bookings అయ్యాయి?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: ఒకటి 1, రెండు 2, మూడు 3, నాలుగు 4, ఐదు 5, ఆరు 6, ఏడు 7, ఎనిమిది 8, తొమ్మిది 9, పది 10, పన్నెండు 12, పదిహేను 15, ఇరవై 20, ఇరవై ఐదు 25, ముప్పై 30, ముప్పై ఐదు 35, నలభై 40, యాభై 50, అరవై 60, డెబ్భై 70, ఎనభై 80, తొంభై 90, వంద 100, నూట యాభై 150. Fractions: అర 0.5, ఒకటిన్నర 1.5, రెండున్నర 2.5, పావు 0.25, ముప్పావు 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Telugu, "ఇరవై ఇరవై ఐదు రోజులు" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ఒక్కటి కూడా లేదు, సున్నా). dispositions.name: bookings_week_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Bookings this week"? The conversation is in Telugu, possibly written in Telugu script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (తెలీదు, తెలియదు, ఐడియా లేదు, finance వాళ్ళకి తెలుసు). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (చెప్పను, చెప్పలేం, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "ఇప్పుడు అమ్ముడుపోతున్న లెక్కన, ఉన్న stock ఎన్ని రోజులు వస్తుంది?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (వారం) = 7 days, a month (నెల) = 30 days; so రెండు వారాలు 14, మూడు వారాలు 21, ఒక నెల 30, నెలన్నర 45, రెండు నెలలు 60. Number words: ఒకటి 1, రెండు 2, మూడు 3, నాలుగు 4, ఐదు 5, ఆరు 6, ఏడు 7, ఎనిమిది 8, తొమ్మిది 9, పది 10, పన్నెండు 12, పదిహేను 15, ఇరవై 20, ఇరవై ఐదు 25, ముప్పై 30, ముప్పై ఐదు 35, నలభై 40, యాభై 50, అరవై 60, డెబ్భై 70, ఎనభై 80, తొంభై 90, వంద 100, నూట యాభై 150. Fractions: అర 0.5, ఒకటిన్నర 1.5, రెండున్నర 2.5, పావు 0.25, ముప్పావు 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Telugu, "ఇరవై ఇరవై ఐదు రోజులు" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ఒక్కటి కూడా లేదు, సున్నా). For example 10-15 days = 12.5 → 13 (not 15), 2-3 weeks = 2.5 × 7 = 17.5 → 18, 1 to 1.5 months = 1.25 × 30 = 37.5 → 38. Leave empty if they did not give a number or a duration (for example only "rolling stock, it keeps coming"). First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (సరే, అవును, హ్మ్, ఓకే), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Telugu or English. The dealer's words may be written in Telugu script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (తెలీదు, తెలియదు, ఐడియా లేదు, finance వాళ్ళకి తెలుసు). declined when they won't say (చెప్పను, చెప్పలేం, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

dispositions.name: stock_days_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Days of stock"? The conversation is in Telugu, possibly written in Telugu script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (తెలీదు, తెలియదు, ఐడియా లేదు, finance వాళ్ళకి తెలుసు). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (చెప్పను, చెప్పలేం, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

dispositions.name: discount_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say the discounts and offers they give customers (company schemes count as offers) are, compared with last week, going up, about the same, or coming down? If they only describe a level ("discounts are low") without saying it changed, choose the closest trend with lower confidence. objective_options.condition: The dealer said discounts and offers went up (for example ఎక్కువ, పెరిగాయి, ఎక్కువ వచ్చాయి, ekkuva).

The dealer said discounts and offers stayed about the same (for example అంతే, అలాగే, same, మార్పు లేదు, ante). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (సరే, అవును, హ్మ్, ఓకే) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said discounts and offers went down (for example తక్కువ, తగ్గాయి, తక్కువ వచ్చాయి, డల్, takkuva). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.

dispositions.name: loan_rejections
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say their customers' vehicle loan rejections, compared with last month, are happening more, about the same, or less? More than last month is high, the same is normal, less is low. If they describe a level instead of a change ("lots of rejections" = high, "normal" = normal), use that. Rejections are about the same as last month, or normal (for example అంతే, normal, నార్మల్, అలాగే).

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (మళ్ళీ call చేయొద్దు). Just declining this time (వద్దు, interest లేదు) is refused. objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.
Declined to take part, or didn't want the call recorded (for example వద్దు, interest లేదు), without asking for a callback or to stop calls.
Asked to be called back at another time, or said the owner or manager isn't available, before the survey started (for example తర్వాత call చేయండి, ఇప్పుడు busy, సాయంత్రం చేయండి).
Asked not to be called again (for example మళ్ళీ call చేయొద్దు).
Not a vehicle dealership, or the wrong business or person entirely (for example wrong number, ఇది showroom కాదు).

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
